name: claude-ai
_why_this_file_exists: The identity a real MCP host announces in its initialize handshake.
RQ3 asks whether a malicious server can tell probe calls from genuine
agent calls. The client feature family is built from clientInfo, so if
probe sessions announced a name the harness invented - the MCP SDK's
default is literally 'mcp' - a classifier would separate the two classes
on that alone and the result would be an artefact of the measurement.
Probe sessions therefore borrow this identity (T17, mimic_host), and the
agent sessions in eval/agent.py use it too.

_provenance.method: Claude Desktop's own MCP subsystem logs each outgoing initialize request verbatim
_provenance.note: Read from existing logs rather than captured by a fresh proxied session. The two are equivalent - this is the same handshake the proxy would have recorded - and it avoids restarting the host. Re-verify by grepping that log for clientInfo.
